beats.story: Sunday morning, I'm awoken in the most horrifying way known. It starts with an insistent knock on my apartment door and a screeched, "Shut up -- is okay." The tone of voice my mom uses only when speaking to my dad. What comes next is a yelled, "Jolene baby! I have brought you some ashe reshteh." My heart stops, and I leap out of bed. Shit! I never texted her! Double shit -- I drank some gin last night and passed out watching a documentary about cruise ships in bed. Why did I have to order all that Chicken on the Way and leave the whole mess in my living room?
beats.story_cn: 周日早晨，我被最骇人的方式惊醒。先是公寓门被敲得震天响，伴随尖叫："闭嘴——没事的。"那是我妈只在对我爸说话时才会用的声调。紧接着是咆哮："乔琳宝贝！我给你带了绿汤面。"我的心跳骤停，猛地从床上弹起。见鬼！我根本没给她发消息！更要命的是——昨晚喝了点金酒，看邮轮纪录片时直接昏睡在床上。为什么非要把"速递鸡"的残羹剩饭堆在客厅不收拾？

beats.story: I throw on a hoodie that I hope covers both my slept-in hair situation and my lost dignity, pile my garbage into the bin, throw the gin bottle and glass under the sink, and do a quick scan to make sure there are no obvious signs that the human embodiment of a bag of merde lives here. There's an empty chip bag on the coffee table, and an old take-out container that still has broth and pieces of wonton wrapper in it on the counter, but other than that, I should be able to get away with medium complaints. I shovel both pieces of garbage into a random cupboard since the bin is full and brace myself. I barely open the door. "What brings you here?" Mom barrels past me with a Tupperware container so huge, she had to have gotten it from a specialty store. "No need to heat this up if you get plates." I should've known this was coming. Every now and then, she shows up with food without warning. I'm sure it's to try to keep me living under a similar regimen as when I was home, like I pretend to be, but unfortunately for us both, shit has veered incredibly off track.
beats.story_cn: 我抓起连帽衫——但愿能遮住睡塌的发型与尽失的颜面，把垃圾堆进桶里，将金酒瓶与杯子塞到水槽下，迅速扫视确保没有"人形垃圾袋居住于此"的明显痕迹。咖啡桌上有空薯片袋，台面还摆着剩汤与馄饨皮的旧外卖盒，除此之外，勉强能逃过严厉指责。我把两袋垃圾铲进任意橱柜——垃圾桶已满，然后屏息凝神。刚把门拉开条缝："什么风把您吹来了？"母亲挤开我冲进来，抱着特大号保鲜盒，非专业超市买不到的那种。"要是有盘子就不用加热。"早该料到。她总突然带食物上门。准是想让我继续过家里那套生活——就像我假装还在过的那样。可惜对我们俩而言，生活早偏航得面目全非。

beats.story: Mom starts toward the kitchen, and I debate following after her to stand in front of the counters and somehow distract from how messy it is, but my dad is hovering awkwardly in the hallway. When we lock eyes, he says, "Sorry to show up like this. I told her to call, but you know." He rocks from foot to foot, as though to demonstrate he's physical standing there against his will. "Come in, Dad." He smiles awkwardly. "I brought my iPad. I can just watch the golf." "Sure." I smile back as best I can. I find Mom in my kitchen, the empty chip bag and wonton container already in each hand. "Jolene, you can't keep soup in the cupboard.
beats.story_cn: 母亲朝厨房走去，我纠结是否该跟去挡在台面前掩饰杂乱，但父亲在走廊尴尬徘徊。我们目光相触时，他说："抱歉这么突然。我让她先打电话的，可你知道的。"他双脚交替重心，仿佛用身体强调是被迫站在这里。"进来吧，爸。"他局促地笑了："我带了iPad，看高尔夫就行。""没问题。"我尽可能挤出微笑。找到母亲时，她正一手抓着空薯片袋，一手举着馄饨盒。"乔琳，汤不能放橱柜。"

beats.story: It goes in the fridge." I snatch them and say, "Thanks, that's a really good hack, but those are garbage. Can you stop opening my cupboards? I'll go through them later. I have a system." But before I can finish, she is in the cupboard under the sink. My overflowing trash can and the three empty bottles of gin sit there like accusations. "Are you really drinking this much?" "No, those bottles are from months ago. And I used some for making sanitizer." My most bonkers lie to date. I scoop them up and gather them against my chest.
beats.story_cn: "应该放冰箱。"我夺过来说："谢了，确实妙招，但这是垃圾。别翻我橱柜行吗？晚点我自己整理。我有固定收纳系统。"话音未落，她已拉开水槽下柜门。溢满的垃圾桶与三只空金酒瓶像罪证陈列。"你真喝这么多？" "不，这瓶子放好几个月了，还拿来做消毒液呢。"堪称我至今最疯的谎言。我一把抄起酒瓶紧抱胸前。

beats.story: "I'll put them in the dumpster." She actually jumps. "Don't throw away, they give money at the depot for this! Albert, come take these bottles for Jolene to get the money." Dad, who is sitting on the couch so awkwardly that it looks like his seat is made of Velcro, says, "I'm sure Jolene can take them in. She's in her thirties." "Yes, I can. And yes, I am, thanks." Mom waves her hand half-heartedly in our direction before setting the bowl of ashe reshteh on the counter and popping off the lid. The glorious smell wafts toward me. She's added so much goat whey and charred garlic that it almost makes everything that's happening right now worth it. Almost.
beats.story_cn: “我把这些瓶子扔垃圾桶去。”她竟真的跳了起来。“别扔！回收站能换钱的！阿尔伯特，快来帮乔琳拿这些瓶子换钱去。”爸爸歪着屁股陷在沙发里，姿势别扭得仿佛椅子长了魔术贴，闷声道：“我确信乔琳自己能搞定。她都三十好几了。”“是，我能。对，我是三十几岁了，谢谢。”妈妈象征性地朝我们挥挥手，把那碗七草粥搁上台面掀开盖子。浓烈香气朝我席卷而来。她加了那么多山羊乳清和焦香大蒜，几乎让眼前这荒唐一幕都值了。几乎。

"Don't worry about cleaning, I'll do it later. You sit and visit." She looks at all ten of my heads.
beats.story_cn: 我盛了一碗啜饮第一口。这是绝佳的醒酒良药。“谢谢你带这个来。”她翻检着我的其他橱柜，连连摇头。“我做了这些，这周你就不用操心午饭了。你得专心工作。清洁用品在哪？这些台面得擦擦。”“别管打扫了，我晚点弄。你坐下聊聊。”她审视着我仿佛长出十个脑袋的窘态。

beats.story: "This place is not something I can stop worrying about. This is not how a polite person lives." She turns to my drawers next, clucking her tongue with disdain. "Why not clean after you eat? What do people say when they visit?" There's no way I've let another human in here -- the place speaks for itself. I take a breath. "Well, normally I'd have some kind of warning. People don't just show up to other people's homes, especially when they're still sleeping." She narrows her eyes. "You were sleeping?
beats.story_cn: “这地方让我没法不操心。体面人可不是这样过日子的。”她随即转向我的抽屉，不屑地啧啧作响。“为什么吃完不收拾？朋友来做客会怎么说？”这地方根本不可能有第二个人踏足——它自己早已说明一切。我深吸口气。“通常我会提前收到通知。没人会不打招呼就登门，尤其当主人还在睡觉时。”她眯起眼睛：“你在睡觉？”

beats.story: It's nine thirty. You could've been studying for your promotion." "I don't think there's going to be a test." Although, given that it's Supershops Incorporated, there will probably be a non-harassment training module with a quiz at the end. She scoffs as she wipes my counter with a cloth that is suddenly in her hands, seemingly produced from nowhere. "It's good to study your job anyways." There's no such thing as winning when the argument is wackadoodle, so I smile and say, "How's your window garden?" "I grow the most beautiful cilantro." Her smile is smug. "Next week, I bring you some." I'm about to interject about her plan to return next week, but I'm just happy to hear she's gardening again. She finishes wiping and shakes her head. "Jolene, this mess is really bad. How come you're living like this?
beats.story_cn: “都九点半了。你本该准备晋升考试的。”“我觉得应该没笔试。”不过按“超级商店公司”的作风，大概率会有反骚扰培训模块附带小测验。她嗤笑一声，不知从哪儿变出块抹布擦起我的台面。“不管怎样熟悉工作总没错。”跟这种胡搅蛮缠的争论本无胜算，我挤出笑容问：“你的窗台花园怎么样了？”“我种的香菜最美。”她得意地扬起嘴角。“下周给你带些来。”我正要插话提她下周再来的事，却已为她重拾园艺而由衷欣喜。她擦完台面摇头叹道：“乔琳，这乱得真够呛。你怎么活得这么邋遢？”

beats.story: It's like you don't care." She says this with all the severity of a doctor making a deadly diagnosis. "Are you okay?" The crease in her brow -- I hate that crease, critical and concerned all at once. I need to curl into a ball. I scramble for some excuse to make it go away. "The problem is that I care too much and don't know where to start." She fake slaps the space between us in a dismissive gesture, her acrylic nails cutting the air like little claws. "Get on with you. It's very serious to be this bad." And to prove her point, she wipes the cloth under a windowsill that I'm pretty sure nobody has ever cleaned in the history of this apartment's construction. "This dust is from long time ago." She hardens her gaze accusingly, and I stiffen -- she is not done with me yet.
beats.story_cn: “简直像你根本不在乎。”她说这话的神态，堪比医生宣判绝症般冷酷。“你还好吗？”她眉间的褶皱——我憎恶那道兼具苛责与关切的褶皱。我只想蜷缩成团。慌忙搜寻借口想抹去这神情。“问题是我太在乎，却不知从何开始。”她虚挥一掌拂过我们之间的空气，那姿态仿佛掸开什么脏东西，亚克力指甲在空中划出利爪般的弧度。“得了吧，把事情搞砸到这种地步才严重呢。”为印证此言，她竟抹向窗台下沿——我敢打赌这处积灰自这公寓建造以来从未被清理过。“这灰尘是陈年旧物。”她目光骤冷如指控，我浑身僵直——她还没打算放过我。

beats.story: "How are you going to have a boyfriend over?" And there it is. She's pushed the exact buttons that set me off. I look toward my dad in some useless, last-ditch plea for help, but he's already absorbed in his iPad. I want to scream. Ever since Ellie's accident, my parents cannot stop managing my every move. And in the aftermath of a town of people sharing the same bad thought about me, all they truly seem concerned about is making sure that I fit the appearance of a perfectly functioning member of society. But I don't want to rehash this same old argument. I say what I need to through clenched teeth.
beats.story_cn: “你还打算带男朋友回来？”终于来了。她精准踩中引爆我的开关。我向父亲投去徒劳的最后求救，他却早已沉浸于iPad的世界。我想尖叫。自从艾莉出事，父母便如影随形监控我的每个举动。而当整个小镇都用同样恶意揣测我之后，他们似乎只在乎我能否维持完美社会成员的表象。但我不想再重蹈这陈旧争吵的覆辙。我咬紧牙关说出必须说的话。

Normally, that kind of accusation would be my cue to curl into myself with shame, bereft with the reminder that I have absolutely no one. Instead, I flash back to my evening drinking milkshakes with Cliff. The ease with which we were able to barb each other. The comfort and warmth between us. It's been a long time since I felt like that. Why does the only person in the world like Cliff have to be the HR guy? In the days since he dropped me off, this world has brutally reminded me how far I am from having anything like that.
beats.story_cn: “我又没想带男朋友回来。”母亲气呼呼道，“你连个朋友都没有吗？”往日这类指控会让我羞愧蜷缩，沉溺于“我孤身一人”的提醒中。但此刻我却闪回与克里夫共饮奶昔的夜晚，那些自然流露的互相打趣，那份松弛温暖的默契。我已许久未有如此感受。为何这世上唯一如克里夫般懂我的人，偏偏是那个人力资源部的家伙？自他送我回家后，现实便残酷提醒我：与这样纯粹的联结，我仍相隔万里。

beats.story: Mom watches me, her lips forming a fine line. "You can have a good life. You can find a good husband. I can help you." She lifts a hand toward my waist, and I freeze, thinking she's going to bring me into a hug. Instead, she pushes past me to wipe the next counter behind us. "This apartment is expensive, and for what? Some dirty carpet and a foozooleh mahaleh neighbor child?" I mean, she does have a point about Miley being nosy, but I'd take her over being under Mom's roof again every time. At least here I have a door.
beats.story_cn: 母亲打量着我，薄唇抿成一条直线。"你能过上好日子，能找个好丈夫，我可以帮你。"她抬手伸向我的腰际，我僵住了，以为她要拥抱我——她却擦身而过，去擦拭我们身后的下一块台面。"这房子租金贵得要命，图什么？发霉的地毯还是那个多管闲事的邻居小孩？"虽然她确实说中了迈莉爱打听的毛病，但我宁愿面对她也不愿再回到母亲的屋檐下。至少在这里，我拥有一扇可以关上的门。

You just need to stop drinking and being sad about things from a long time ago." My lips tremble. Mom's prescription for me is always just to literally stop being sad. I know it's not malicious. She grew up believing that depression and anxiety are controllable with the right attitude, fruit, and sunlight.
beats.story_cn: "我在这里挺好的，"我对她说，话语挤在发紧的喉咙里显得细弱。她的声音软下来："你就该过得好。你眼看就要升职了，只要别再喝酒，别总为陈年旧事伤神就行。"我的嘴唇颤抖起来。母亲给我开的处方永远是直白的"别难过了"。我知道她没有恶意。她成长的环境让人相信：只要心态端正、多吃水果、多晒太阳，抑郁和焦虑都是能控制的。

There's only one way to put this conversation to bed. So I do what I've always done: push past every thought inside my head and every sinking feeling inside my soul, and say, "You're right. Starting tomorrow, I'm going to be better." I snatch the cloth from her fingers and pat her shoulder. "Don't worry about cleaning. I've been wanting to clean this place. I want to have people over." Again, I'm back to the milkshakes -- to Friday.
beats.story_cn: 她自己那些早被搁置的创伤，在我这一堆麻烦加入之前就已存在。作为移民，这是生存模式。让这场对话落幕的唯一方式，就是故技重施：压下所有翻腾的念头与下沉的心绪，开口说道："您说得对。从明天起，我会变好的。"我从她指间抽走抹布，拍拍她的肩膀："别操心打扫了，我早想把这地方收拾干净，想请朋友来坐坐。"我又回到了奶昔话题——回到了星期五。

Mom is still staring at me with narrowed eyes, so I continue: "And drinking isn't even fun. I'm starting to suspect it might be unhealthy even." She rests her fist on her hip. "Even drinking a little can cause wrinkles and damage to your heart." "I don't want that. I'll be happier if I stop, I think. That's probably the problem." She nods. "I hear it's a depressant." "That makes so much sense." Mom nods, placated for now.
beats.story_cn: 为何每次我以为自己开始好转，就轻易倒退回昨夜那副惨状？这真是我吗？母亲仍眯眼盯着我，我继续说道："而且喝酒根本不好玩。我现在怀疑它可能还有害健康。"她将拳头抵在腰侧："就算少喝点也会长皱纹，损伤心脏。""我可不想那样。戒酒了我应该会更快乐，我想。这大概才是症结。"她点点头："听说酒精会抑制情绪。""确实很有道理。"母亲颔首，暂时被安抚住了。

beats.story: She's never one to deny an easy answer when it is gifted to her. "Make sure you finish the bowl. It's very healthy." I smile and take another hefty spoonful of the ashe reshteh, letting the comforting, familiar flavors wash through me. "I'll put the rest in the fridge." Once Mom gathers everything, including Dad and his iPad, she turns to me and whispers, "The girl with the dirty fingernails that let us in is still outside. Should we call her mom?" Oh god. I peer out the window and see Miley's mousy head leaning against the wall in the hallway. "Don't worry about her. That's normal." But as soon as I say it, she shifts, sinking lower -- she's just sitting there by herself?
beats.story_cn: 她向来懂得顺手接住送上门的台阶。“记得把这碗吃光，可有营养了。”我微笑着又舀起一大勺波斯蔬菜浓汤，任那熟悉温厚的滋味在唇齿间漫开。“剩下的我放冰箱。”待母亲收拾好所有碗碟，连同抱着平板的父亲一同劝离后，她转身对我低语：“刚才给我们开门的那个指甲脏兮兮的女孩还在外头。要叫她妈妈来接吗？”天哪。我探向窗外，看见米莉灰扑扑的脑袋正倚在走廊墙边。“别管她，小孩子都这样。”可话音刚落，她身子一歪，顺着墙根滑坐下去——她竟独自坐在那儿？

She shuffles nervously from leg to leg. There's a little hole in her Toms, and it's how small her pinkie toe still is that chips into me. "Sorry if we were being loud." She shrugs, indifferent. "I could hear you arguing with your mom about your life inside your apartment." I let out a sigh. "Yeah, next time could you not let her in?
beats.story_cn: 内疚如潮水般漫上心头。父母微笑着打开门，经过她时尴尬地保持沉默。“嘿，米莉，”我唤道，“还好吗？”“挺好的。”她紧张地来回挪动双脚。那双Toms帆布鞋破了个小洞，而她小脚趾那依然纤弱的尺寸刺痛了我。“抱歉我们刚才太吵了。”她无所谓地耸耸肩，“我在外面能听见你和妈妈在屋里为人生争吵。”我叹了口气。“是啊，下次能不能别让她进来了？”

beats.story: She needs to call before." Miley's hands curl tightly against her chest. She must be having a terrible day, and it's not even noon. "Sorry," she says. "I thought I was helping." I shake my head. "It's okay. It's just my mom is . . ." Actually, I don't need to go there with her.
beats.story_cn: “她下次得先打电话。”米莉的双手紧紧攥在胸前。她今天肯定糟透了，而时钟还没走到正午。“对不起，”她说，“我以为我在帮忙。”我摇摇头。“没事。只是我妈妈……”算了，没必要和她解释这些。

beats.story: "What are you doing out here? I mean, in my hallway?" "I came to give you this." She holds out a hand, and I notice for the first time that she is holding a mess of black and white yarn. "Your birthday gift." I eye it warily. It looks like a bunch of loose black and white strings tied together, with two googly eyeballs glued onto the situation, seemingly on purpose. Is this a prank where I have to pretend to think it's beautiful, and then she laughs at me? "It was meant to be a zebra," she clarifies. Miley chews her hangnail, insecure as she waits for me to respond, and my heart tumbles like a domino. That's why she wanted to know my favorite animal.
beats.story_cn: “你在这儿干嘛？我是说，在我走廊里？”“我来给你这个。”她伸出手，我这才注意到她手里攥着一团乱糟糟的黑白毛线。“你的生日礼物。”我警惕地打量着它。看起来就是一堆散乱的黑白线绑在一起，上面还粘着两颗咕噜转的眼珠子，显然是故意的。这是不是那种我得假装觉得漂亮，然后她就会笑话我的恶作剧？“本来想钩成斑马的，”她解释道。梅莉咬着手指边的倒刺，等我反应时显得局促不安，我的心像多米诺骨牌一样塌陷下去。这就是她想知道我最喜欢什么动物的原因。

I'm still learning." The faint light in her eyes -- I've seen it slowly begin to dim lately. "Hey, Miley, what are you . . .

beats.story: Is your mom around?" Her eyes shift downward, giving me the answer I don't want. I'm woefully ill-equipped for this. "She had to work a double," Miley says to the carpet that hasn't been vacuumed in decades. "I was supposed to ask a friend to go over, but everyone was busy, so I'll just hang out." It's the insecure little fists. "Don't worry, I'm not that young. It's fine." The little gift presses down heavily in my palms. "I know." It's technically true; she's old enough to be alone for a few hours. "So, what are you going to do today?" "I guess I have more crocheting to do." She looks at me -- and damn it, I recognize that faint glimmer in her expression.
beats.story_cn: “你妈妈在吗？”她目光下垂，给了我一个不愿面对的答案。我对此毫无招架之力。“她得连上两个班，”梅莉对着那块几十年没吸尘过的地毯说。“我本来该找朋友过来的，但大家都忙，所以我就自己待会儿。”是那双不安的小拳头出卖了她。“别担心，我没那么小了。没事的。”那份小小的礼物在我掌心沉甸甸的。“我知道。”从年龄上说确实如此；她已够大，可以独自待上几个小时。“那，你今天打算做什么？”“我猜……我得再钩点东西了。”她看向我——该死，我认出了她眼神里那抹熟悉的微光。

beats.story: I take an infinitesimal step backward into my apartment's threshold without thinking, and just like that the glimmer fades. I nod. "Well, if you need anything -- uh, I mean, if something happens, please knock. And if I'm not around -- " She smiles, cheeky. "You'll be home." I press my own smile on and return to my apartment to finish the weekend out, determined that next week I will focus on my plan and not let myself be distracted by anything. Or anyone. Milkshake hangovers are simply not worth the angst.
beats.story_cn: 我下意识地朝自己公寓门内缩了一小步，那一抹微光立刻消失了。我点点头。“嗯，如果你需要什么——呃，我是说，如果有什么事，就敲门。如果我不在——”她狡黠地笑了笑。“你会在的。”我硬挤出一个微笑，转身回公寓过完这个周末，决心下周要专注于自己的计划，不再让任何人或事分心。奶昔的后劲，可不值得这般心神不宁。
